synopsis: Mining3 delivered ACARP project C26028 in January 2021 as a proximity-detection testing framework; it is a shared physical test protocol, not a simulator [f15627, f16088]. Its two-tier structure proves object detection in Tier 1 before testing Level 8 or Level 9 advisory or intervention action in Tier 2 [f15625, f15628, f559]. The booklet recommends this sequence for the collision mitigation project's physical test campaign, while warning that choreographed tests cannot replace site-specific, multi-variable dynamics [f15634]. The baseline is explicitly limited to choreographed scenarios and excludes pre-existing site controls and complex, multi-variate dynamic vehicle interactions [f347, f560, f561, f15629]. Despite these limitations, the booklet groups C26028 with the Mining3 toolkit, NIOSH evaluations and MOSH verification as sources of comparability and credible independent evidence [f682, f15630].
